strongest_angle: Detail the terms of the October 2026 $800 million legal settlement between the Archdiocese of New York and approximately 1,300 parishioners, marking the second-largest payout involving a Catholic archdiocese in the United States.

key_facts.fact: The Archdiocese of New York agreed to an $800 million settlement with about 1,300 parishioners who alleged sexual abuse by clergy, marking the second-largest payout involving a Catholic archdiocese in the United States.
Jeff Anderson, a lawyer representing more than 250 of the plaintiffs, stated that the settlement was finalized pending signed paperwork.
Archbishop Ronald Hicks sent an email on Saturday, October 24, 2026, to clergy confirming the settlement agreement.
The legal claims were brought under New York's Child Victims Act and lookback laws following more than seven years of litigation.

quotes.text: The Archdiocese of New York and attorneys for about 1,300 parishioners who said they were sexually abused by clergy have agreed to an $800 million settlement of their legal claims, the second-largest involving a Catholic archdiocese in the U.S.
quotes.speaker: John Hanna

quotes.text: The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay $800 million to settle the claims brought against the church by some 1,300 people who say they faced sexual abuse from clergy members and lay workers.
quotes.speaker: Chandelis Duster
